subject: Pilot and ramp pricing request — CareBridge
messages:
From: Anita Shah <anita.shah@carebridge.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: CareBridge Procurement <procurement@carebridge.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot + long-term pricing ask

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. CareBridge is ready to move from the proof-of-concept into a 6–9 month pilot with explicit ramp commitments. A few key points from our side:

- Pilot expected to start Nov 1 and run 9 months.
- Committed usage: ~1.2B tokens month 1 rising to ~3.6B tokens by month 6.
- Goal is to convert to a multi-year enterprise contract at the end of the pilot.

To make this economics work for CareBridge, Procurement is requesting a 28% discount off list Hosted API usage pricing for the duration of the pilot (with a negotiated step-down after conversion). They will sign an SOW if we can confirm the rates and the billing cadence.

Attaching the draft SOW and our Q3 usage report for context. Please let me know what you can commit to and any contract caveats you need.

Anita
Anita Shah
Director, Strategic Partnerships
CareBridge Health

Attachments: CareBridge_SOW_v3.pdf (application/pdf), usage_report_Q3.csv (text/csv)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Anita Shah <anita.shah@carebridge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot + long-term pricing ask

Hi Anita — appreciate the detail and the attachment. Quick read-through and a couple clarifying points:

- We can cover a pilot with committed volumes but 28% is outside our standard hosted usage concession band for self-serve-to-enterprise.
- Standard enterprise onboarding discounts typically land in the 10–18% range depending on volume and term. Anything >20% requires senior commercial approval.

Ben / Karthik — I’ve flagged this as an escalation because CareBridge’s ramp profile looks strong and the opportunity to convert to enterprise is real, but their ask (28% for pilot duration) needs an exec decision. I’ve attached a note with the baseline numbers and their SOW. Can you review and advise recommended negotiation levers (time-limited ramp, credit structure, caps, or usage floors)?

Anita — can you confirm whether CareBridge needs the 28% to be applied immediately (month 1) or if a staged ramp would be acceptable (e.g., 25% first 3 months, 28% month 4–9)? That will affect our financial modeling.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@carebridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot + long-term pricing ask

Looping in my commercial take:

- CareBridge projected ARR at enterprise conversion looks compelling (~$2.1M ARR on conservative conversion assumptions).
- If we do a time-limited pilot concession, risk is short-term revenue dilution but large net-new ARR possibility.

Options I recommend for Exec consideration:
1) Approve a 25% concession for the pilot (9 months) with a mandatory conversion review and minimum ARR target to maintain the rate.
2) Approve a sliding concession: 28% months 4–9, 20% months 1–3; Redwood retains right to revert to list if usage drops below 80% of commit.
3) Approve 28% only if CareBridge signs a 24-month volume commitment post-pilot (not likely).

Financials: incremental gross margin impact at 25% over 9 months is tolerable given CLTV; anything above 25% materially increases payback risk unless paired with guarantees.

Recommend we escalate to Mina Haddad for sign-off on any concession >25%. If Mina wants, we can add a carve-out that the concession is limited to Hosted API (no embeddings at that rate) and includes monthly usage gates.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Anita Shah <anita.shah@carebridge.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec escalation: CareBridge pilot — request for approval above standard concession band

Mina — forwarding the thread and our analysis. TL;DR: CareBridge (strategic enterprise prospect) is asking for a 28% discount on Hosted API usage for a 9-month pilot that starts Nov 1. They show a strong ramp to ~3.6B tokens/month and signal multi-year conversion intent.

Why escalation:
- 28% exceeds our usual delegated approval limits. Ben models that 25% is the maximum comfortable concession without a revenue guardrail; 28% materially increases CAC payback risk.
- CareBridge is sensitive to up-front economics; they may walk if we don’t meet their ask.

Recommended ask for Exec: please approve one of the following options (circle/answer):
A) Approve 28% for the full 9-month pilot (CareBridge signs SOW and monthly commitment).
B) Approve up to 25% for the 9-month pilot with mandatory conversion targets and monthly gates; allow Ben/Priya to negotiate 1–2 points more on performance milestones.
C) Approve 24% for 9 months with a hard reversion clause to list prices if usage falls below 80% of committed volumes.

Attached: redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx (impact models) and usage_report_Q3.csv from CareBridge.

Need an answer by end of day Friday (Oct 22) to hit procurement timelines.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Anita Shah <anita.shah@carebridge.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Exec escalation: CareBridge pilot — request for approval above standard concession band

Team — reviewed the materials and Ben’s modeling. CareBridge is a strategically valuable prospect and I don’t want us to lose momentum, but we must protect unit economics. I approve a constrained concession to bridge the pilot:

Decision: Approve a 24% Hosted API usage concession for the 9-month pilot, with the following caveats (must be captured in the SOW / commercial terms):
- Monthly committed floors and a right to revert to list pricing if usage falls below 80% of committed volumes for two consecutive months.
- Concession applies only to Hosted API calls (no bundled embeddings/other add-ons at that rate).
- Finance to apply a one-time credit cap (ceiling) limiting total cumulative discount value to the modeled exposure in redwood_pricing_sheet.xlsx.
- Contract must include a 30-day conversion review and executive check-in; any further concession requests require Director+ sales approval.

This gives the field some concession room (above 20%) while limiting long-term dilution and requiring operational guardrails. Priya/Ben — you have my sign-off to tell Procurement yes on 24% with the caveats above and to proceed to DocuSign once legal has updated the SOW.

Mina Haddad
VP, Sales | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: none
